propositions: The primary Mirror Guard watcher (mirror-guard.yml workflow) fails on a single instantaneous sample of expected transient Gerrit-GitHub replication lag (~15s post-submit), while the module's design docstring delegates lag absorption to the alarm layer's sustained-divergence window

The secondary watcher (CloudWatch monitoring_ws7.tf) correctly implements the designed sustained-divergence evaluation window (2x5-min) to suppress transient lag, but the primary workflow watcher has no equivalent window

Adding an in-process, scheduler-agnostic persistence wrapper to run() that re-samples up to 3 times with 45-second spacing will allow transient divergence to self-converge within the window while keeping persistent divergence failures loud
The convergence-on-success test case (fetch sequence [diverged, in-sync]) must exhibit exit 0 with a healthy verdict and exactly 1 fetch + 0 sleep calls when the lag window absorbs the transient lag
All non-converging failure paths (static GitHub tip, moving never-converging tip) must remain exit 1, and missing-SHA must fail immediately without re-sampling

The module's own introduced commit d96628c9dca shipped both the design text requiring alarm-layer absorption and the incomplete workflow implementation, classified as plan-defect caused by scope-of-work omission
